trigger.snippet: - `MELIAN_EVAL_MISSES`: a JSON array of `{ name, repo, base, head, file, rule?, alternativeRules?, fix?, lines? }`, each a valid miss that a review of record found and Melian missed, in a clone on the machine. `lens` mode measures a miss one of whose rules `trust-boundary` declares; `whole` mode and the parity measurement measure any. `fix` names the commit that fixed it; `lines` is the first and last line of the defect at the head. A sighting under `rule` or any of `alternativeRules` can find the miss. A miss may leave out `rule` only when it has `lines`, and then a sighting under any rule at those lines finds it; `alternativeRules` needs a `rule`. Each rule must be one some lens of the base's `full` tier declares for the file, in either mode, so one misses file serves both and a misspelt alternative exits 2. In `lens` mode one of them must be `trust-boundary`'s. A miss is scored on the reviewing lenses' own sightings at the head, `trust-boundary`'s in `lens` mode and every lens check's in `whole`, read from the review's store level by level, because a finding merged with another lens's, or with another level's, keeps only its speaker's lines and words. An ID excludes lines, so quick and careful can sight one ID at different lines, and the verifier can refute one and uphold the other. A sighting answers the miss when the verdict holds the claim of its check, ID and level unrefuted, it sits at the file under one of the miss's rules, or any rule when it names none, and it overlaps those lines. The claim may sit in any of the verdict's groups, so a refuted one scores the miss as not found. A dismissed claim counts by its own verification, since the measurement asks whether the lens sighted the defect and the verifier let it stand, and a dismissal is a person's later call that a fresh store cannot hold. A sighting the verdict holds no claim for, a reviewing lens's claim with no sighting, or a claim the verdict holds twice, leaves that miss with no score, as a failed review does. The score follows the verdict: an unrefuted claim counts whether or not its probe was sound, and the results file is what lets a reader check. Without `lines`, they come from git's diff of the head against the fix: the old side of each hunk in the miss's file, and for a pure insertion the line before it and the line after. A fix that changes nothing in the file exits 2 before any provider. Only a hand-entered `lines` range scores a miss, found or missed, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-16, given in the coordinator's session. A fix's diff says which lines changed, not which defect each line held: one hunk can repair two touching defects, and several hunks can repair more than the miss. So a location from a fix decides nothing. It matches as `fix hunks`, and whenever an unrefuted sighting sits at the file under the rule, the miss prints as unadjudicated, naming every hunk and the ones the sightings overlap; give the miss `lines` to adjudicate it. A miss with neither matches by file and rule alone, the same way. An unadjudicated miss may hold another defect's sighting, so its review gets no score, as a failed review gets none, and its pass gets no miss recall. A review that sighted nothing at the file under the rule still scores as missed. A miss scores, found or missed, only when the review's own telemetry shows a completed conversation of a responsible lens, other than a prober's, whose stored coverage holds the miss's file, and which saw the defect. The responsible lenses are those the review runs that cover the file and declare one of the miss's rules, or all of them when it names none. `whole` mode scores only a miss with hand-entered `lines`, since its other lenses sight more of the file than the miss, and exits 2 before any provider, naming each miss without them. Each lens stage carries the `coverage` its conversation's stored policy gave it, and core's `lensCovers` answers. It also carries `shown`, the head path of each file whose diff its prompt carried whole, and `read`, the head lines `read_file` delivered to it for each changed file, as the transcript reader that counts review coverage finds them. A lens saw the defect when `read_file` delivered it a line inside the miss's lines, or when the prompt showed it the file and a head-side hunk of the range's diff holds one of those lines. The miss's lines are its hand-entered `lines`, or else the head lines its fix changes, so a fix-located miss with no sighting scores as missed only where the lens was shown or read a line the fix changes. The diff has no context lines, so a block shows only the lines its hunks change, and a pure deletion shows no head line. For a miss with neither `lines` nor `fix`, a shown file or any line `read_file` delivered counts. A prompt past its 200 KB limit stops before the block that would cross it, so a diff block is shown whole or not at all, and a file whose block was cut counts as not shown. A `search` result counts for nothing, since it delivers lines the lens asked about by pattern, not the code around them. A review where no responsible lens saw the defect prints the miss as unadjudicated with no score and says why, lens by lens: `not run` for a lens with no completed conversation scoped to the file, and `never shown` for one whose conversations were neither shown the file nor read the lines, so the report can tell a lens that saw the defect and missed it from one that never saw it. A stage an older Melian wrote has no `shown`, so its misses print as unadjudicated unless the lens read the lines. The goldens are not affected: the largest golden's whole head is about 41 KB.
